_comment: Tier-2 Layer-C: skfem poisson numerical-correctness gate. Mirrors fenics/poisson_mms_convergence. Runs the catalog-recommended skfem API surface (MeshTri.refined, Basis with ElementTriPk, BilinearForm + LinearForm, condense, solve) end-to-end against the manufactured solution u = sin(π·x)·sin(π·y), f = 2π²·sin(π·x)·sin(π·y) on [0,1]². Asserts P1 h=1/32 L2 error <= 5e-3, P2 <= 5e-5, P3 <= 5e-7, P1 EOC h=1/16 → h=1/32 in [1.7, 2.3]. CROSS-BACKEND NUMERICAL AGREEMENT with fenics: P1=1.31e-3 vs fenics P1=1.32e-3, P2=7.14e-6 vs fenics P2=7.14e-6 (identical to 4 sig figs), EOC=1.993 vs fenics 1.993. Verified against skfem 12.0.1 on 2026-06-01. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): This is a correctness gate, so the mutation breaks the discretisation the gate certifies rather than removing a pitfall. T2_MUTATE=1 drops the manufactured load constant LOAD_CONST from 2.0 to 1.0, so the load is pi^2 sin(pi x) sin(pi y) instead of 2 pi^2 sin(pi x) sin(pi y) and f no longer equals -Delta u; the computed field is half the exact one. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 5 expect_in_output strings (P1 1.31e-03, P2 7.14e-06, P3 5.87e-08, EOC 1.993). Because the expectations here are bare key prefixes that match any value, the evidence is a forbidden string APPEARING rather than an expectation disappearing: T2_MUTATE=1 gives P1 2.51e-01, P2 2.50e-01, P3 2.50e-01 and EOC 0.010, printing 'FAIL:' four times, so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
